previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: John, a homeless man with a history of hypertension and alcohol abuse, was admitted after a fall following heavy alcohol consumption. He was found to be in atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate, likely due to noncompliance with his previous metoprolol regimen. His heart rate was poorly controlled with beta-blockers but responded to diltiazem, which was started in the hospital and continued at discharge. Evaluation revealed no acute intracranial or shoulder injuries, and chest pain was deemed musculoskeletal. He showed no signs of alcohol withdrawal and received supportive supplementation with thiamine, folic acid, and multivitamins. He was discharged home with medication adherence counseling, new prescriptions, and follow-up arranged with community health services.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo male with history significant for atrial fibrillation with 
RVR and ETOH abuse presents with atrial fibriallation with RVR 
and alcohol intoxication.
.
ACTIVE ISSUES
-------------
# Atrial fibrillation with RVR: CHADS2 score 1.  Patient has 
been difficult to rate control on recent admissions, and 
responds best to diltiazem.  Patient responded poorly to maximum 
doses of diltiazem over the course of this admission, and was 
eventually better controlled to HR 110s on diltiazem and 
metoprolol.  Precipitants of patient's atrial fibrillation 
include ongoing alcohol use, as well as pneumonia that was found 
on this admission.  Patient was placed on aspirin 325 mg for 
anticoagulation.  TSH was checked on recent admission and found 
to be normal.  Patient triggered multiple times while admitted 
for tachycardia.  He was monitored on telemetry during his 
admission.  He was discharged on diltiazem XR 480 mg PO daily 
and metoprolol succinate PO 75 mg daily, as well as full dose 
aspirin.  Patient was counseled to stop drinking, as this is 
almost certainly precipitating his problem.
.
# Multifocal pneumonia: aspiration vs. HCAP, with associated 
pleural effusion R>L.  Patient triggered for transient 
desaturation down to the low ___, responsive to oxygen 
supplementation.  Chest CTA was obtained showing no pulmonary 
embolism, but evidence of multifocal pneumonia and bilateral 
pleural effusions.  Radiologic finding also could be explained 
by chemical pneumonitis based on initial O2 desaturation and 
subsequent fevers.  He was placed on vancomycin, cefepime and 
metronidazole.  Upon discharge, he was transitioned to 
amoxicillin/clavulanate to complete a total seven day course.  
Blood and urine cultures were still pending at discharge.
.
# Chest pain: patient reported ___ chest pain in the ___ 
his chest on admission, described as sharp and radiating down to 
his abdomen.  Chest pain occurred intermittently during his 
hospitalizatoin.  Cardiac biomarkers were negative x 3 and ECG 
remained unchanged throughout admission.  Chest x-ray was 
generally unremarkable and CTA of the chest showed no pulmonary 
embolism but evidence of multifocal pneumonia and pleural 
effusions.  Differential included alcohol-induced gastritis, 
multifocal pneumonia.  Patient was given magic mouthwash and 
omeprazole for gastrointestinal symptoms.  He was discharged on 
omeprazole for treatment for possible gastritis.
.
# Abdominal pain: patient complained of ___ epigastric and 
periumbilical pain, associated with nausea, and sharp in 
character.  Benadryl/lidocaine/Maalox washes improved the 
patient's symptoms.  Differential diagnosis included 
alcohol-induced gastritis, pancreatitis, and other 
intraabdominal processes.  Lipase was checked and not 
appreciably elevated.  Liver function tests suggested 
alcohol-induced injury.  A CT abdomen was obtained and noted 
mesenteritis.  It was noted in the report that HIV infection 
could result in such findings.  An HIV test should be performed 
as an outpatient in the near future.  Omeprazole was initiated 
and continued on discharge for the patient's symptoms of pain.  
Symptoms of pain ceased by the time of discharge.
.
# Alcohol intoxication: Patient 1.5 pints of vodka before 
admission with ethanol level of 379.  He received thiamine and 
folate in the emergency department, and was maintained on these 
medications during the hospitalization and on discharge.  
Patient was placed on a CIWA scale and required diazepam dosing 
during his hospitalization.  Patient reports no history of 
previous delirium tremens or withdrawal seizures.  CIWA scale 
has been progressively decreased.  Social work and psychiatric 
liaison consult was obtained to discuss possible section 35, for 
which patient was not deemed a candidate.  Patient was advised 
to cease alcohol use as it is likely the cause of his medical 
issues.
.
# Transaminitis: AST:ALT > 2:1 on admission consistent with 
alcohol-induced liver injury, bilirubin level was normal.  This 
likely represents alcohol-induced liver injury from ongoing 
alcohol use.  Patient was advised to cease alcohol use as it is 
likely the cause of his medical issues.
.
# Hypertension: patient is being discharged on diltiazem and 
metoprolol, mostly for rate control.  Blood pressure was 
monitored regularly and patient was discharged on diltiazem and 
metoprolol.
.
INACTIVE ISSUES
---------------
# Depression: patient reportedly, via his PCP, has history of 
depression and was previously on citalopram.  Patient should 
have follow-up with psychiatry, to be arranged by his primary 
care provider.
.
TRANSITION OF CARE
------------------
# Follow-up: patient will follow up with his primary care 
provider upon discharge.  He should be referred to psychiatry 
for follow-up of his depression.  He should likely have an HIV 
test after discharge due to the finding of mesenteritis on 
abdominal CT scan.  He should have a follow-up chest X-ray 6 
weeks after discharge to assure resolution.  A follow-up of his 
control of heart rate and alcohol use is needed.  There are 
pending blood and urine cultures at the time of discharge which

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___ 

Comparison is made with a prior study from ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ man with dyspnea, assess for CHF.

FINDINGS:  AP portable upright view of the chest was provided.  Low lung
volumes again limits the evaluation.  There is persistent moderate
cardiomegaly without overt CHF.  There is subtle opacity in the right medial
lung base which could represent crowded bronchovasculature though the
possibility of a subtle pneumonia is difficult to exclude.  Pneumothorax is
seen.  Minimal blunting of the left CP angle could indicate a small effusion. 
Bony structures appear intact.

IMPRESSION:  
1.  Cardiomegaly, no overt CHF, tiny left effusion.  
2.  Probable bronchovascular crowding resulting in subtle increase in opacity
at the right medial lung base.  Lateral view would aid to confirm.

INDICATION:  Chest pain, shortness of breath with new hypoxia, evaluate for
PE.  Abdominal pain.  Evaluate abdomen and pelvis.

COMPARISON:  CTA chest and abdomen, ___.

FINDINGS:  Evaluation of the lung parenchyma is somewhat limited by low volume
inspiration, but some multifocal nodular opacities are present (2:23) in the
left upper lobe, (2:27) in the left lower lobe and to some degree in the right
lower lobe (2:32).  Bilateral pleural effusions, right greater than left are
present and new.  The appearance of the airways is normal.  Multiple
mediastinal lymph nodes are present, the largest conglomeration of subcarinal
lymph nodes measures up to 12 mm in short axis and prevascular nodes measure
up to 11 mm.  Numerous axillary lymph nodes are present, but not
pathologically enlarged.

On the angiographic study, the aorta and pulmonary arteries appear normal.  No
pulmonary embolism is identified.  No pericardial effusion is present.  No
significant coronary artery calcifications are present.

Bibasilar atelectasis is present adjacent to the effusions.

ABDOMEN:  Similar to the previous examination, although slightly more
prominent are multiple enlarged retroperitoneal lymph nodes.  There is slight
stranding of the retroperitoneal fat.  However, the spleen, adrenals,
pancreas, gallbladder, and liver all appear within normal limits.  The kidneys
enhance and excrete contrast symmetrically without masses, or hydronephrosis. 
No free air, or free fluid is present.  The stomach and abdominal loops of
bowel appear normal.

PELVIS:  Several enlarged pelvic nodes and mesenteric lymph nodes are also
present.  No free air or free fluid is present.  Pelvic loops of bowel appear
normal.  The bladder and prostate appear normal.  Numerous inguinal lymph
nodes are present, however, none are particularly pathologically enlarged.

BONE WINDOWS:  No suspicious bony lesions are identified.  Mild degenerative
changes are present in the lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Multifocal nodular opacities in bilateral lungs, with bilateral pleural
effusions, right greater than left.  Findings are concerning for developing
multifocal pneumonia.  Repeat chest radiograph should be performed to assess
for resolution after appropriate treatment.
2.  No pulmonary embolism.
3.  Slight progression in retroperitoneal adenopathy and slight fat stranding.
Findings are nonspecific but could indicate mesenteritis and may also be seen
in HIV.
Findings were discussed with Dr. ___ at 8:30 p.m. on ___.
